messages:
sara: Hi team — customer Jane (Acme) opened an escalation: streaming responses on /v1/chat generate are showing p99 total-time regressions over last 48h. They say TTFB looks okay but streams hang mid-chunk for long pauses, inflating p99. attaching their repro and logs below.

customer-jane: repro curl we used:
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-13b","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long prompt causing many tokens"}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
We get first chunk within ~80ms but then the next chunk sometimes delays 400–1200ms. Happens on us-west and eu-west. Not every request, more at p99 and p999.

support-bot: Alert: streaming.p99_total_time_us in us-west increased by 3.2x vs baseline (48h). Correlated with small spike in chunk_coalesce_ms.

aj: Thanks — can you paste a plain example of the raw bytes you see? also what client (node/python) and whether they're using SSE or h2-streaming?

customer-jane: Node fetch + EventSource polyfill (SSE). Client code is a normal fetch with readable stream piping to event parser. I can attach a small sample of the raw chunks: 
```
> chunk: {"delta":"Hello"}
> chunk: {"delta":" world"}
# pause 640ms
> chunk: {"delta":"!"}
```
We see the 640ms gap frequently at p99.

leo: Noted — this looks like chunk coalescing/flush heuristics at the proxy/edge. If the runtime is batching tokens for GPU efficiency and the proxy is also coalescing small writes, we can get mid-chunk delays when traffic pattern changes.

mike: I pulled service logs for the timeframe. Sample log lines showing flush latency: 
```
[2026-02-09T21:12:03.123Z] req=abc flush_candidate=true token_count=6 flush_wait_ms=480
[2026-02-09T21:12:03.604Z] req=abc flush_emitted=true emitted_tokens=2
[2026-02-09T21:12:04.150Z] req=xyz flush_candidate=true token_count=4 flush_wait_ms=1020
```
This aligns: the runtime sometimes defers flushes when tokens are sparse to batch for throughput, but that hurts streaming p99.

aj: Quick mitigation options:
- For customer: recommend non-streaming path (stream=false) which currently avoids intermediate flush waits — they accept higher immediate latency but lower jitter.
- Runtime-side: add a temporary per-customer override to lower the flush_coalesce_ms threshold (e.g., from 200ms -> 25ms) for Acme. Needs feature flag plus canary.
- Edge-side: disable proxy coalescing for SSE responses or set TCP_NODELAY for these routes.

sara: Customer prefers to keep streaming (UX important). They asked for a short-term workaround before we roll runtime change. Can we offer a tenant-level header to force more aggressive flush?

mike: We have an internal header x-redwood-stream-priority used in some tests to force immediate flush. I'll expose a support-only header to Acme today and patch the gateway to honor it for their API key. That should reduce mid-chunk gaps.

aj: I'll prepare a small runtime patch to reduce coalesce window behind a feature flag and run a canary in us-west with 5% traffic for 1 hour, monitor streaming.p99_total_time and emitted-chunks-per-second. If stable, ramp.

leo: Also add an instrumentation counter for "flush_wait_ms > 200" per request so we can alert before customer hits p99.

sara: Timeline and comms plan:
- Today: enable x-redwood-support-flush=immediate for Acme API key (support action) — low-risk gateway change.
- Within 24h: aj deploys runtime canary with reduced flush window. Monitor and rollback if errors.
- Follow-up: if coalescing still causes issues, we may add a streaming fallback header that forces sync-mode for the route.

customer-jane: thanks — we'll try the header. can you notify when enabled?

support-bot: Action created: TICKET-4982 (Acme streaming p99) assigned to aj,mike — priority P1.

mike: Done — support header enabled for Acme API key (x-redwood-support-flush=immediate). Please verify and paste any fresh traces.

customer-jane: Verified — much better. earlier p99 was ~2.3s, now p99 ~430ms on same test. Will continue to monitor and report.

aj: Thanks — starting canary in us-west now. Will post results in 30m.

sara: Great. I'll update the customer and keep thread open until canary is validated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
